statements.text: The crossing came from the numerator: from 492,600 to 492,700 the path's 64-row output rose x2.006 while the real change rose x1.0065.
The output layer's weight size rose x1.0079 over the same 100 model steps; a weight-size change of that amount scales the output by the same factor on unchanged hidden activations.
The 492,700 output is row-varying: its rows' shared mean vector is 2.3% of its squared size, so it is not a fixed vector of the M9 kind.

A doubling between two reports is within this gauge's measured spread: x2.01 is the largest of 31 report-to-report factors of the span; the next three are x1.95 at 491700, x1.92 at 490200, x1.86 at 491200; B1E's five largest were x2.58, x1.83, x1.76, x1.65, x1.63.
The next report fell back x0.82 (share 0.847).
The level under the gauge rose slowly: the median share was 0.450 over B1E (486,000-489,350) and 0.556 over the span; the output layer's weight size went 0.0305 -> 0.0343 -> 0.0373.

The 492,700 gauge rows were unusual in the paths' shared input: the proprioception slot's row-to-row spread read 0.997, the largest of 33 reports (median 0.890); the audio slot's was also the largest.
Two other paths rose on the same rows: vestibular x1.51, vision x1.69; tactile x0.95, audio x1.37.

The separate-sample error readings did not worsen at 492,700: the next-frame lesson's window ratio read 0.667 (492,600 0.710, 492,800 0.737) and the hold-first audit 0.644 (492,600 0.917, 492,800 0.608); 0 = exact, 1 = no better than predicting no change.

That does NOT imply the output rises x1.0079 on unchanged hidden activations: the weight directions and the bias matter, and a general weight and bias change can alter alignment and cancellation while barely changing the root mean square. posture.points_scale: a body's change in POINTS = 100 x the mean over the 7 ruled parts of that comparison's part differences (later minus earlier): the content score's 0-1 scale on a 0-100 scale; negative = the later encoder lower.
posture.note: Read-out measurements of how well a fixed reader reconstructs posture from each encoder's tokens; the comparisons' earlier and later encoders are named per entry. Not evidence of a shared cause with M6, and no loss is called irreversible here.
